value: Finally, TSA provided no responses and burden hours for watch list matching and watch list resolution.  TSA has taken steps to reduce and eventually end the requirement for airport operators to conduct watch list matching and related watch list matching resolution, transitioning from 76 respondents reported in the last ICR submission to 0 respondents.  In 2018, a TSA policy change transitioned most airport operators to a TSA system (eSecure Flight**) that conducts those functions on a daily and/or as needed basis.  In 2021, a separate TSA policy change transitioned the remaining 76 airport operators to a TSA system (Transportation Vetting Portal**) that performs perpetual watch list matching on the airport operator’s behalf.  After the 2021 policy change was completed, no airport operators have conducted watch list matching and related watch list matching resolution.

value: In 2011, the National Air Trade Association (NATA) charged a fee for this service ranging from $29 to $75.
